subject: Request: staged financial holdback and conditional termination option
messages:
From: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@medsync.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production SLA — remedies beyond credits

Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. MedSync is moving quickly on the integration; two quick procurement items surfaced from compliance and finance during the contract review: one is straightforward (data retention clarification), the other is more substantive on SLA remedies.

Summary of MedSync ask (high-level):
- If Redwood misses P1 availability / sustained latency SLOs more than X times in a rolling 90-day window, we need an option to terminate without penalty and a graduated financial holdback that offsets migration and regulatory risk.
- We’re not asking for unconstrained liquidated damages, but something beyond simple monthly credits — a staged financial charge that scales with repeat breaches, with the ability to cure once per incident.

Why this matters: our service supports patient-facing triage; regulators expect stronger contractual levers for repeated production failures. Finance also wants a quantifiable mitigation if we must transition to an alternate provider.

I’ve attached the compliance note and a redline from procurement showing the proposed remedy table and a 3-strike termination trigger. Happy to take a call to walk through.

Can you confirm if Redwood would consider a compromise structure (staged holdback + cure windows + termination after consecutive breaches)?

Appreciate it,
Ari
MedSync — Senior PM, Integrations
Attachments: MedSync_SLA_Remedy_Request_20270903.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@medsync.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production SLA — remedies beyond credits

Ari — thanks for the clear note and the materials. We understand the sensitivity here and want to be cooperative given MedSync’s regulatory profile. High-level response: we are open to a structured compromise but cannot agree to open-ended, uncapped damages or immediate termination for a single incident.

Proposed commercial compromise (initial):
- Staged financial holdback: up to 3% of monthly committed fees held in a reserve after the first qualifying repeat P1 event, increasing to 6% after the 2nd repeat inside 90 days, and 10% after the 3rd. Holdback would be applied to the next invoice cycle and can be drawn to cover documented migration costs if termination is exercised within the cure timetable.
- Cure windows: each P1 event triggers a 14-day cure period during which we will prioritize remediation, provide runbooks and an incident RCA. If the root cause is fixed and corrective actions validated, the holdback is released in full.
- Termination: termination right only after three qualifying repeat P1 breaches in a rolling 90-day window, and only if the holdback has been applied and the cure windows have been exhausted.
- Caps and limits: aggregate financial exposure capped at the total of three months’ committed fees; no punitive multipliers.

We will circulate a redline that reflects this structure and a short carve-out for force majeure and third-party cloud outages. Can we schedule a short sync next week to review the markup? I’m looping Vivek to help on capacity/ops specifics.

Best,
Neha
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@medsync.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: MedSync Procurement <procurement@medsync.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production SLA — remedies beyond credits

Neha — thanks for the quick reply and the proposed structure. A few points from procurement/finance after an internal read:
- The tiered holdback idea is reasonable, but finance asks that the holdback be escrowed with a neutral third party rather than simply applied as a credit on the next invoice. This is to ensure funds are available if we must pay a replacement provider.
- The aggregate cap at three months’ committed fees is acceptable if it’s on top of credits and limited to documented migration costs. We need clearer definitions of what qualifies as a P1 that counts toward the "three" (duration thresholds, regional impact, percentage of traffic impacted).
- Regarding force majeure and cloud provider outages: MedSync will accept a carve-out for true force majeure, but vendor self-inflicted capacity constraints should not be excluded.

I’ve attached a short procurement summary with suggested edits to the remedy table (lines called out). Can you have legal take a look at the escrow ask and the P1 definition? If Redwood is open to escrow for the holdback and a narrow P1 definition that includes duration and percent-traffic thresholds, we can move quickly.

—Ari
Attachments: MedSync_SLA_Remedy_Summary_20270906.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@medsync.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2027 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production SLA — remedies beyond credits

Ari / Neha — looping in Legal and Contracts. Appreciate the pragmatic tone. We can agree to a narrowly-scoped escrow for the staged holdback under the following guardrails:

Redwood counter-proposal (legal summary):
1) Escrow mechanics: Redwood will place the holdback amounts into an interest-bearing escrow with an escrow agent agreeable to both parties. Funds are released to MedSync only upon: (a) mutual agreement that migration is required; or (b) a final arbitral determination that Redwood materially breached the SLA after the cure periods. If neither condition occurs within 12 months of the holdback, funds revert to Redwood.

2) P1 definition (narrowed): event qualifies if all three are true:
   - sustained > 5 minutes of unavailability for a replicated service endpoint in a region;
   - impacts >= 20% of MedSync’s traffic to Redwood or causes degradation of a core patient-facing pathway; and
   - confirmed by Redwood monitoring and MedSync incident correlation within 48 hours.

3) Cure and remediation: each qualifying event triggers a 14-day cure; Redwood will provide RCA, mitigation plan and, where requested, prioritized engineering support. If remediation is accepted by MedSync within the cure window, escrow is released in full.

4) Termination: termination right available only after three qualifying events in a rolling 90-day window where escrow has been applied and cure windows exhausted. Upon termination Redwood will cooperate with an orderly offboarding and provide exported logs/configs; migration costs eligible under escrow are limited to documented third-party transition vendor invoices.

5) Caps: aggregate escrowed exposure limited to three months’ committed fees; this is exclusive of standard SLA credits. No punitive multipliers; no uncapped indemnity.

If MedSync accepts these guardrails, Legal will prepare a concise contract exhibit that captures the mechanics and the escrow agent selection process. Happy to hop on a call to walk Ari and procurement through the arbitration release conditions.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Counter_Terms_20270906.docx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production SLA — remedies beyond credits — internal decision request

Team — summary and ask below. I briefed MedSync on Marissa’s counter and they’re generally receptive; procurement raised the escrow requirement as a hard ask but seemed willing to accept the 12-month revert clause. Two items I need help confirming before we send a final exhibit:

1) Operational: Vivek — can ops commit to the detection / confirmation SLA (48-hour correlation) and the support cadence during the 14-day cure window? Also need an estimate of how often this detection threshold might be reached in our current capacity models for MedSync’s expected traffic (we have their projected q1 usage).

2) Commercial/legal: Karthik/Marissa — are you comfortable with the arbitration release condition for escrow release (arbitral determination if disputed)? If not, propose alternatives (e.g., neutral third-party technical arbiter). Also confirm the definition of "documented migration costs" we will accept (third-party invoices only? including customer internal FTE?)

MedSync is asking to sign quickly if we accept escrow; this is a material deal (annual committed spend ~$1.2M). I recommend we accept the escrow with the 12-month revert clause provided ops and legal sign off on detection and the narrow P1 definition.

If you agree, I’ll ask Legal to generate the exhibit and set a short sync with MedSync procurement tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Neha
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
